content.text:
Confirmed: `SystemProperties.getInstance().getSystemProperty()` reads from a bundled `system.properties` resource file (which only contains build metadata like `product-version`, `product-build`, `git-commit`), not JVM system properties. Since `exist.home` is a JVM system property (set via `-Dexist.home=...` or similar), looking it up via `SystemProperties` instead of `System.getProperty` means it would never be found there and would always log `"unknown"`.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: c342cbc05e44f776f0055b8182abbf4550a6c459

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** The fix commit reverted the "eXist Home" log line from `SystemProperties.getInstance().getSystemProperty("exist.home", "unknown")` back to `System.getProperty("exist.home", "unknown")`, while leaving the version/build/git-commit lines (which legitimately use `SystemProperties`) untouched. I ran `git log -p --follow` on `JettyStart.java` and searched for every occurrence of the buggy `SystemProperties.getInstance().getSystemProperty("exist.home", ...)` pattern across the file's history to find where it was first introduced. The earliest occurrence traces back to commit `c342cbc0` (2011-04-19).

**(2) Specific change:** That commit introduced the new `SystemProperties` class (a singleton that loads a bundled `system.properties` resource file containing build metadata like `product-version`, `product-build`, `svn-revision`/`git-commit`) and refactored the startup logging to use it instead of a manually-loaded `Properties` object. In doing so, it also changed the "eXist Home" line from the correct `System.getProperty("exist.home")` (a JVM system property set at runtime) to `SystemProperties.getInstance().getSystemProperty("exist.home", "unknown")` — incorrectly treating `exist.home` as if it were part of the build-time properties file.

**(3) Evidence:** Viewing the new `SystemProperties.java` added in that same commit shows it only loads `system.properties` from the classpath resource and has no knowledge of JVM system properties. Since `exist.home` is never written into that resource file (it's set via `-Dexist.home=...` at JVM startup), every lookup since this commit would fall through to the `"unknown"` default — exactly the symptom fixed by the 2016 commit restoring `System.getProperty("exist.home", "unknown")`.

I'm confident in this identification: the fix is a direct, scoped revert of this one commit's mistake for the single "exist.home" line, with no other intervening changes to that line found in the file's entire history.
